Subject: Renewal planning — branching tenancy + temporary staging cluster

Hi Neha,

Quick context: our renewal for MedTerra Analytics is due 2026-11-01. Over the last 9 months we've hit a sustained uplift across ingest and analytics scoring — peak token throughput during batch windows is ~1.6M tokens/min and our nightly scoring job frequently tops out the host pool. We want to:

- Add a lightweight staging cluster to validate new model variants before promoting to prod.
- Split one tenant into a dedicated VPC segment for regulatory reasons (PHI scope) — that will require isolated clusters and different retention settings.
- Confirm cost/term implications for committing to additional dedicated capacity at renewal.

I've attached a short workbook with our recent traffic slices and a proposed growth curve (MedTerra_MA_plan_v2.xlsx). Can Redwood provide a recommended rollout pattern (staging -> graduated capacity -> tenancy split) and a draft amendment that aligns with our renewal window?

Happy to hop on a 30 min sync this week — Emily (Ops) and I are available Tue/Wed afternoons PT.

Thanks,
Emily

Hi Emily — thanks for the workbook and the clear asks. Summary of what I heard:

1) short-term: add a staging cluster (isolated, lower-cost profile) to validate model releases without impacting prod;
2) medium-term: split the PHI tenant into a dedicated VPC segment with its own clusters and retention/compliance controls;
3) commercial: you want options for committing to additional dedicated capacity at renewal and the associated term adjustments.

Proposed technical rollout (high level):
- Week 0–2: provision staging cluster (single node pool, pre-quantized model variant) + prefix/KV cache config; validation checklist (smoke + 95th pct latency).
- Week 3–6: promote staging variants behind a canary route, enable KV prefix caching for shared prefixes, monitor token-cost impact.
- Week 7–10: provision PHI VPC tenant clusters (two-node primary + one standby across zones), apply KMS policies, run compliance audit hooks.

Commercially, we can do a graduated capacity commitment: a 12-month base commit (existing term) with a staged addendum that activates additional reserved capacity on day 45 after kickoff. That lets you minimize upfront commit while getting a favorable blended rate for capacity added at renewal. Vivek — can you confirm discount tiers and a sample amendment text? Lauren — can you take point on the staging validation checklist and expected SLOs we should include?

I can do Tue 10/13 at 1:30pm PT for a 30 min sync — is that good for you?

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Director, Redwood Inference

- Term options: 12-month auto-renew or 18-month with an additional 5% discount and prioritized capacity at peak windows (useful given your batch peaks).
- Deal mechanics: we'll draft an amendment that adds an activation clause ("Activation Window: day 1–60 post-kickoff; activation executed on written notice") and a List of Clusters to be provisioned (staging, PHI-prod-primary, PHI-standby).
